intent_en: To demonstrate that carbon dioxide is the primary source of global greenhouse gas emissions, thereby justifying the necessity of stopping its release to limit climate change.
previous_intent: To illustrate that carbon dioxide is the dominant source of global man-made greenhouse gas emissions, emphasizing the necessity of reducing fossil fuel combustion to mitigate climate change.
narration_support: Carbon dioxide, which is emitted when we burn fossil fuels, accounts for most of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.
chart_support: Pie chart illustrating the composition of global man-made greenhouse gas emissions, with Carbon dioxide occupying the vast majority of the chart.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly identifies CO2 as the main culprit and states the need to stop releasing it. The chart visually confirms CO2 is the dominant component (the large red slice) of the emissions breakdown.
